verdict.executive_summary: A low-severity user-reported phish alert fired because Maryam Iqbal used the Report Phishing button on a newsletter from newsletter@marketwatchdaily.example at 2026-08-29T08:31:00Z. Available evidence indicates this was a legitimate subscribed marketing email sent from a long-established benign sender to 62 internal recipients, with no attachment, a clean marketing URL, and no clicks or replies. This matters only as a user-report event; there is no evidence of malicious email activity or user impact.
verdict.rationale: Playbook coverage exists for user-reported phishing. The detection itself only claims that a user reported an email, not that phishing occurred. Required checks were completed: sender history shows three years of incident-free mail; all sender-authentication checks passed; the domain is consistently benign across all configured TI feeds; the message had no attachment and only one normal marketing URL; the same newsletter was delivered to 62 recipients as a normal subscription; mail logs confirm nobody clicked or replied; and the same sender has been reported six times before with harmless outcomes and no later misclassification. The specific innocent explanation is that Maryam Iqbal did not recognise the sender name and reported a legitimate subscribed newsletter, which is directly supported by the user statement and the mail characteristics. The deciding fact is whether the reported message was in fact a legitimate subscription newsletter rather than a phishing lure; that fact was obtained from sender history, authentication results, recipient pattern, content, and prior identical harmless cases, and it supports the innocent explanation. No hard trigger applies, no watchlist or crown-jewel context is present, all enrichment sources answered, and the alert meets the Wave 1 close condition for marketing mail with clean URL/no attachment and no clicks or replies. This is therefore a Close as False Positive: the rule correctly detected a report action, but the reported email is not malicious and not what a phishing investigation needs escalated for.

verdict.executive_summary: A user in Finance reported a phishing email on 2026-08-29 that impersonated Northbank Accounts Payable and targeted recipients with a credential-harvesting link and a disguised executable attachment. The sender domain is newly registered, failed all sender-authentication checks, and both the domain and attachment are confirmed malicious by multiple intelligence sources. No user clicked or submitted credentials, but the campaign reached 14 Finance and Procurement recipients, so this requires Tier 2 handling for response and broader remediation.
verdict.rationale: This alert type has a playbook entry and was triaged under Playbook §6 user-reported phishing. The detection itself only proves that a user reported an email, not that the email was malicious, so the content had to be assessed separately. The email is malicious on multiple independent grounds: it spoofed an internal finance function, the sender domain was only 11 days old and had no prior contact history, SPF/DKIM/DMARC-equivalent sender identity checks all failed, safe detonation of the URL showed a pixel-perfect Northbank sign-in clone that exfiltrates entered credentials, and the attachment hash is known malicious and associated with HTML smuggling. Threat intelligence from all configured feeds links the domain and file to a known banking credential-harvesting campaign. The playbook says to always escalate if the message targets finance, which it did, and closure is not permitted because the URL and attachment are not clean. No evidence shows successful compromise yet: nobody clicked and the reporting user did not enter credentials. This is therefore a true positive phishing event requiring Tier 2 investigation and response, not a benign or false positive.
